# Inbound pharmaceutical imports from outside the EU: Value and Weight
```{r}
#packages
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```
```{r}
#organize raw data set
eu_raw <- read_csv("EU import monthly.csv",
  na = c("", "NA"),
  col_types = cols(
    ..default = col_character(),
    OBS_VALUE = col_double()
  )
)

#organize it by order follow by reporter - partner - product - import - month

eu_new <- eu_raw |>
  dplyr::select(
    freq, reporter, partner, product, flow,
    TIME_PERIOD, indicators, OBS_VALUE
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = indicators,
    values_from = OBS_VALUE
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    import_kg = QUANTITY_KG,
    import_eur = VALUE_EUR
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    month_date = as.Date(paste0("01-", TIME_PERIOD), format = "%d-%b-%y"),
    year = as.integer(format(month_date, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(month_date, "%m"))
  )|>
  dplyr::arrange(reporter, partner, product, flow, month_date)
#spotcheck: year date
stopifnot(!anyNA(eu_new$month_date))
names(eu_new)
head(eu_new$month_date)
class(eu_new$month_date)

eu_new <- eu_new |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$month_date >= as.Date("2018-01-01"),
    .data$month_date < as.Date("2026-01-01")
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(partner, month_date)

eu <- eu_new
```
```{r}
eu_total <- eu |>
  filter(
    reporter == "EU27_2020",
    partner == "EXT_EU27_2020",
    product == "54",
    flow == "1"
  ) |>
  arrange(month_date)


plot_data <- eu_total |>
   filter(year %in% 2018:2025) |>
   mutate(
    month = as.integer(format(month_date, "%m")),
    import_billion_eur = import_eur / 1e9
   )

plot_data |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    months = n_distinct(month),
    available_values = sum(!is.na(import_eur)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


plot_data$time_month <- (
  (plot_data$year - 2018) * 12 +
  plot_data$month - 1
)
eu_model <- lm(
  import_billion_eur ~ time_month,
  data = plot_data
)
summary(eu_model)
confint(eu_model)

plot(eu_total$month_date, eu_total$import_eur/ 1e9,
      pch = 16, xlab = "Month", ylab = "Import Value (billion EUR)")

smoothed <- ksmooth(
  x = eu_total$month_date,
  y = eu_total$import_eur/ 1e9,
  kernel = "normal",
  bandwidth = 100
)
lines(smoothed, col = "#8b0806", lwd = 2)

baseline_fit <- predict(eu_model, newdata = plot_data)

lines(x = plot_data$month_date, y = baseline_fit, col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
```

```{r}
#identify specific month in 2020 that is under 2019 import level
change_data <- plot_data |>
  filter(year %in% c(2019, 2020)) |>
  select(month, year, import_eur) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = import_eur,
    names_prefix = "year_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    change = (year_2020 - year_2019) / 1e9
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

ggplot(change_data, aes(x = factor(month), y = change)) +
  geom_col(
    aes(fill = change >= 0),
    width = 0.65,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black") +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = sprintf("%+.2f", change),
      vjust = ifelse(change >= 0, -0.4, 1.4)
    ),
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#2166AC", "FALSE" = "#B2182B")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in EU pharmaceutical imports",
    subtitle = "2020 minus the same month in 2019",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Change in import value (billion EUR)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

```

Use Regression Discountinuity to examine the new EU phharmeceutical stratagy effect
Set the cut off dat at "2020-07-01" for the first aknowledge, and "2020-11-01" for officail publish

```{r}
cutoff_july <- as.Date("2020-07-01")
cutoff_nov <- as.Date("2020-11-01")

plot_data <- plot_data |>
  mutate(post_july = as.integer(month_date >= cutoff_july))

plot_data |>
  filter(
    month_date >= as.Date("2020-01-01"),
    month_date <= as.Date("2021-01-01")
  ) |>
  select(month_date, post_july)

```
draw cutoff line and jump at the point post_july
```{r}
jump_data <- plot_data |>
  mutate(
    t = (as.integer(format(month_date, "%Y")) - 2020) * 12 +
      as.integer(format(month_date, "%m")) -7,
    post_july = as.integer(month_date >= cutoff_july),
    post_nov = as.integer(month_date >= cutoff_nov),
    slope_july = pmax(0, t),
    slope_nov = pmax(0, t - 4),
    y = import_eur / 1e9
  ) |>
  arrange(month_date)

july_model <- lm(y ~ t * post_july, data = jump_data)

boundary <- data.frame(
  t = c(0, 0),
  post_july = c(0L, 1L)
)

heights <- predict(july_model, newdata = boundary)
july_jump <- unname(heights[2] - heights[1])

before_jump <- jump_data |>
  filter(post_july == 0) |>
  select(month_date, t, post_july) |>
  bind_rows(data.frame(
    month_date = cutoff_july,
    t = 0,
    post_july = 0L
  )) |>
  arrange(month_date)

after_jump <- jump_data |>
  filter(post_july == 1) |>
  select(month_date, t, post_july) |>
  arrange(month_date)

before_jump$fit <- predict(july_model, newdata = before_jump)
after_jump$fit <- predict(july_model, newdata = after_jump)

summary(july_model)

two_cutoff <- lm(
  y ~t + post_july + post_nov + slope_july + slope_nov,
  data = jump_data
)

summary(two_cutoff)


```
RD model with cutoff line at JULY 
This extimate when the pharmaceutical stratagy started public cunsaltaton, how it effected to import.

model with two cutoff line, July for public consalutation, and Novenber for offical published
the R-squared only increased 0.0035, showing that the effects change was smaller than when during the public consalutation.
```{r}
#calculate the gap of jump
line_data <- data.frame(
  month_date = c(
    min(jump_data$month_date), cutoff_july,
    cutoff_july, cutoff_nov,
    cutoff_nov, max(jump_data$month_date)
  ),
  t = c(min(jump_data$t), 0, 0, 4, 4, max(jump_data$t)),
  post_july = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  post_nov = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1),
  period = rep(1:3, each = 2)
) |>
  mutate(
    slope_july = pmax(0, t),
    slope_nov = pmax(0, t - 4)
  )

line_data$fit <- predict(two_cutoff, newdata = line_data)

cutoff_data <- data.frame(
  date = c(cutoff_july, cutoff_nov),
  before = line_data$fit[c(2,4)],
  after = line_data$fit[c(3,5)]
)
```
```{r}
ggplot(jump_data, aes(x = month_date, y = y)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, color = "black") +

    xintercept = c(cutoff_july, cutoff_nov),
    color = "#911c1c", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

    data = line_data,
    aes(x = month_date, y = fit, group = period),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 1

  ) +

    title = "EU Pharmaceutical imports",

  ) +
```

# Regression results

Coefficients are followed by conventional OLS standard errors in parentheses.
Significance levels: *** p < 0.01; ** p < 0.05; * p < 0.10.

```{r regression-tables, echo=FALSE}
format_coef <- function(model, term, scale = 1) {
  coefs <- coef(summary(model))
  if (!term %in% rownames(coefs)) return("")
  p <- coefs[term, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  stars <- if (is.na(p)) "" else if (p < .01) "***" else if (p < .05) "**" else if (p < .10) "*" else ""
  sprintf("%.3f%s (%.3f)", coefs[term, "Estimate"] / scale,
          stars, coefs[term, "Std. Error"] / scale)
}

# Convert the baseline's reported coefficients and SEs to billion EUR.
# Its time regressor remains monthly, as in the original fitted model.
baseline_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Constant", "Time trend (per month)", "Observations",
                "R-squared", "Adjusted R-squared"),
  Baseline = c(format_coef(eu_model, "(Intercept)"),
               format_coef(eu_model, "time_month"),
               nobs(eu_model), sprintf("%.3f", summary(eu_model)$r.squared),
               sprintf("%.3f", summary(eu_model)$adj.r.squared)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(baseline_table, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Baseline time trend (Monthly Extra-EU Pharmaceutical Import Value (billion EUR))")

models <- list("July cutoff" = july_model, "November cutoff" = nov_model,
               "Two cutoffs" = two_cutoff)
labels <- c("Constant", "Time trend (per month)", "July level change",
            "November level change", "July slope change",
            "November slope change")
terms_by_model <- list(
  c("(Intercept)", "t", "post_july", NA, "t:post_july", NA),
  c("(Intercept)", "t", NA, "post_nov", NA, "t:post_nov"),
  c("(Intercept)", "t", "post_july", "post_nov", "slope_july", "slope_nov")
)
cutoff_table <- data.frame(Statistic = c(labels, "Observations", "R-squared",
                                        "Adjusted R-squared"))
for (i in seq_along(models)) {
  model <- models[[i]]
  cutoff_table[[names(models)[i]]] <- c(
    vapply(terms_by_model[[i]], function(term) {
      if (is.na(term)) "" else format_coef(model, term)
    }, character(1)),
    nobs(model), sprintf("%.3f", summary(model)$r.squared),
    sprintf("%.3f", summary(model)$adj.r.squared)
  )
}
knitr::kable(cutoff_table, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Cutoff models (Monthly Extra-EU Pharmaceutical Import Value (billion EUR))")
```

The dependent variable is the monthly value of EU27 imports of medicinal and pharmaceutical products (SITC 54) from non-EU countries, measured in billions of euros (EUR). The sample covers January 2018 to December 2025 (96 monthly observations). Time is centered on July 2020 in the July and two-cutoff models, and on November 2020 in the November model. Constants therefore refer to different reference dates. Blank cells indicate terms excluded from a model. Slope changes are measured in billions of EUR per month. Coefficients are reported with conventional OLS standard errors in parentheses. Statistical significance does not establish causality.
